bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Your Construction Management Salary

When you're negotiating a construction management salary, it helps to see the full picture: what you'll earn each year, each fortnight, and what's left after tax and super. This guide explains how to convert an hourly rate to an annual figure using a standard 38-hour week, and how tax and super fit in.

### The Basic Formula: Hourly × Hours × 52

The simplest way to estimate your annual gross pay is:

**Annual gross = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

For a full-time role, we assume 38 hours per week (the standard under the Fair Work Act). If you work more or fewer hours, adjust accordingly. This formula gives a straight-line estimate – it doesn't include overtime, penalty rates, or allowances.

For example, if your hourly rate is $60.00:
- Weekly: $60.00 × 38 = $2,280.00
- Fortnightly: $2,280.00 × 2 = $4,560.00
- Annual: $2,280.00 × 52 = $118,560.00

### The Fortnightly View

Many Australian employers pay fortnightly. Your fortnightly gross is simply your weekly gross multiplied by two. Using the example above, $2,280.00 per week becomes $4,560.00 per fortnight. This can help you budget and compare with job advertisements that quote fortnightly pay.

### What About the Construction Management Salary Average?

The Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) reports that full-time adult ordinary time earnings in the construction industry averaged $1,985.30 per week in May 2026. That is an industry average, not a job median for construction management. Your actual construction management salary depends on your experience, location, and the specific role. Use the hourly conversion to work backwards from a salary offer or forward from your current hourly rate.

### National Minimum Wage vs. Award Rates

The Fair Work Commission sets the National Minimum Wage. From 1 July 2026, it is $26.44 per hour ($1,004.90 per week for 38 hours). For casual employees, the minimum includes a 25% loading, making it $33.05 per hour. However, most construction management roles are covered by awards or enterprise agreements that pay above the minimum. Check the relevant award on the Fair Work Ombudsman website or refer to our [pay guides](/blog) for more details.

### Casual Loading and Superannuation

If you are a casual employee, your hourly rate should include a 25% casual loading. When using our [timesheet](/), you can check a box to add 25% casual loading on top of your base rate. Never type a rate that already includes casual loading – the tool adds it for you.

Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings at 12% (from 1 July 2026). It is not deducted from your pay; your employer contributes it separately. The super guarantee applies up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. For a construction management salary of $118,560, the super contribution would be $14,227.20 per year.

### Estimating Tax on Your Construction Management Salary

Tax is calculated using the 2026–27 resident tax rates:
- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus the Medicare levy of 2% (generally). The Medicare levy reduction thresholds for singles are based on 2025–26 figures as 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed at the time of preparation. This estimate does not include HELP repayments, the Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging.

For a $118,560 annual salary:
- Tax on first $18,200: $0
- Tax on $18,201 to $45,000 ($26,800): $4,020 (15%)
- Tax on $45,001 to $118,560 ($73,560): $22,068 (30%)
- Total tax: $26,088
- Medicare levy (2% of $118,560): $2,371.20
- Total tax and Medicare: $28,459.20
- Net annual pay: $90,100.80
- Net fortnightly: approximately $3,465.42

### Important Notes and Limitations

This estimate assumes:
- The same hourly rate every week
- No unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances
- No salary sacrifice
- Super at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top
- Tax using the 2026–27 resident scale with full tax-free threshold
- Medicare levy using 2025–26 single reduction thresholds (not confirmed for 2026–27)

For a more detailed breakdown, see our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) guide. You can also check the [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page for current rates.

### Using the Timesheet Tool

Our [timesheet](/) allows you to enter your base hourly rate and optionally add 25% casual loading. It then calculates your weekly, fortnightly, and annual gross pay. Remember, the annual figure is hourly × hours per week × 52, assuming a 38-hour week unless you adjust the hours. The tool does not deduct tax or super – it gives you the gross amounts before those deductions.

### Final Thoughts

Whether you are negotiating a construction management salary or checking an offer, converting your hourly rate to annual, fortnightly, and weekly figures gives you clarity. Use the industry average as a reference point, but remember it is an average, not a median for your specific job. Always check your award or agreement for the correct minimum rates and consult the Australian Taxation Office for personalised tax advice.

For more resources, visit our [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page or the [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) guide.
